builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Where Should the Code Go? Locating Foundation-Model Errors in Bitemporal Inventory Simulation
summary: Replaces free-form LLM reasoning over raw bitemporal reports with exact canonicalization before the model call and exact deterministic rollout after it, in an exactly solvable inventory simulation. Costs engineering effort to build the canonical input layer and exact continuation code, plus interface care since forced-answer calls can disable reasoning or exhaust output budgets on some model-provider pairs. Can fail if the wrong remedy is applied (canonicalization does not fix rollout errors and vice versa), if the model is already at ceiling, or if the tool-calling interface confounds reasoning evaluation.
rationale: For teams using third-party APIs on state-tracking tasks with revisions, offloading exact deterministic substeps to code is cheap to implement, but the dominant error source is model-dependent so workload-specific validation is required.
technique: Deterministic code wrapping for bitemporal state and rollout

claims.statement: Replaces free-form LLM reasoning over raw bitemporal reports with exact canonicalization before the model call and exact deterministic rollout after it, in an exactly solvable inventory simulation. Costs engineering effort to build the canonical input layer and exact continuation code, plus interface care since forced-answer calls can disable reasoning or exhaust output budgets on some model-provider pairs. Can fail if the wrong remedy is applied (canonicalization does not fix rollout errors and vice versa), if the model is already at ceiling, or if the tool-calling interface confounds reasoning evaluation.
Canonical input removes report-selection error; exact continuation removes rollout error; neither repairs the other; strong models are at ceiling on raw reports.
